ablūtum: sonship, the status of a son (Harper’s word, from ablum “son”): ina ablūtim (ab-lu-tim) “from sonship”; nasāḫim ina ablūtim “to cast out of sonship”
aḫāzum-Š: Š-stem of aḫāzum “to take”: to make take, have (a man) take (a wife): ušaḫḫazūšu (u-ša-aḫ-ḫa-zu-šu) “they shall have him take (a wife)” (present plural + -šu “him”)
biblum: what is brought, a present (Harper); the gift sent at a betrothal, separate from the tirḫatum “bride-price”: biblam (bi-ib-lam) “a present” (accusative)
dâkum-Š: Š-stem of dâkum “to kill” (the causative; Harper’s third stem): to have (someone) killed: ušdīk (uš-di-ik) “she has had (her husband) killed”
eliāt: beyond, over and above (before a genitive): eliāt zittišu (e-li-a-at) “over and above his share”
emum: father-in-law (the bride’s father): emišu (e-mi-šu) “of his father-in-law”, bīt emišu “the house of his father-in-law”; emim (e-mi-im) genitive; emušu (e-mu-šu) “his father-in-law” as subject
gašīšum: stake, pole (Harper): ina gašīšim (ga-ši-ši-im) “on a stake”; to set a person on one is to impale
kabtum: heavy; grave (of an offence): arnam kabtam (kab-tam, accusative) “a heavy offence”
kallatum: bride (for a son), written with the Sumerogram É.GI₄.A, three signs and no ending written (Harper’s transliteration adds the ending, kal-lâtam): kallātam “a bride”
karāṣum-D: UNCERTAIN: D-stem of karāṣum, Harper’s “to slander”: uktarriṣṣu (ug-dar-ri-zu) “he has slandered him” (perfect + -šu “him”, ṣ + š said ṣṣ, spelled with ZU); the verb is rare and the form is not secure, the sense is Harper’s
lamādum: to learn, to know; of a person, to know carnally (Harper): iltamad (il-ta-ma-ad, perfect) “he has known (his daughter)”; ilmassi (il-ma-zi) “he has known her” (preterite ilmad + -ši “her”, d + š said ss, spelled with the sign ZI); ilmassima (il-ma-zi-ma) “has known her, and”
nasāḫum: to pull out, uproot; of a son, to cast out, disinherit (Harper: “to cut off, to disinherit”): nasāḫim (na-sa-ḫi-im, infinitive) “to cast out”; anassaḫ (a-na-za-aḫ) “I shall cast out” (first person present); inassaḫ (i-na-za-aḫ) “he shall cast out” (third person present)
nasāḫum-N: N-stem of nasāḫum, the passive: to be uprooted, cast out (of a family house): innassaḫ (in-na-az-za-aḫ) “he shall be cast out”
palāsum-D: UNCERTAIN: D-stem of palāsum, Harper’s “to look with longing”: uptallisma (up-ta-al-li-is-ma) “he has looked longingly (at another woman), and” (perfect + -ma); the verb is rare
wabālum-N: N-stem of wabālum “to carry”, the passive (Harper: passive, IV 1, of “to bring”): ibbablušum (ib-ba-ab-lu-šum) “(what) was brought to him” (preterite + the subjunctive -u of a ša-clause + -šum “to him”)
šinā: two (šinā); šinīšu (ši-ni-šu) “his second (time)”: adi šinīšu “up to his second time”, i.e. a second time
ḫarāṣum: to cut off, deduct (Harper: “to deduct”): iḫarraṣma (i-ḫar-ra-aṣ-ma) “he shall deduct, and” (present + -ma)
ḫiārum: to choose; to betroth (Harper; the verb behind ḫīrtum “wife”): iḫīrma (i-ḫi-ir-ma) “he has chosen (a bride), and” (preterite + -ma)

__broaden__.aḫāzum: to take, grasp; Š-stem šūḫuzum “to make take hold” · to take (a wife): iḫuz (i-ḫu-uz) preterite, iḫuzma “he took, and”; present iḫḫaz (i-iḫ-ḫa-az) “he shall take”, which also serves as a permission, “he may take”; iḫḫazu (i-iḫ-ḫa-zu, with the subjunctive -u) “(before) he takes”; infinitive aḫāzim (a-ḫa-zi-im), taking its object in the genitive; taḫḫazanni (2nd person, with -anni “me”) · to take (a wife): iḫuz (i-ḫu-uz) “he has taken (a wife)”, iḫuzma, itaḫazma (i-ta-ḫa-az-ma, perfect + -ma) “he has taken, and”; present iḫḫaz “he shall take”, aḫḫaz “I shall take” (a-ḫa-az, the doubling not written), taḫḫaz “you shall take”; iḫzu (iḫ-zu) with the relative -u: ša aššatam lā iḫzu “who has not taken a wife”; iḫḫazzi (i-iḫ-ḫa-az-zi) “he shall take her” (-ši, z and š merged)
__broaden__.-ši: her / it (3rd-person feminine singular suffix, on a verb): ukannūšima “they shall convict her”, inaddûši “they shall throw her”, iqallûši “they shall burn her” · iṣṣabassi (iṣ-ṣa-ba-az-zi) “it has seized her” (the t of the perfect + -ši said ss, spelled -zi) · on the present plural: imannûši “they shall count her”, ibaqqarūši “they shall claim against her” · on the Š-stem: ušērribši “he shall bring her in”, ušamṭaši “he has belittled her” · on a verb, the object “him” (UNCERTAIN): inaddûši “they shall throw him” (§155, the man being thrown into the water; the plate shows the sign ši, which elsewhere is “her”) · ilmassi (il-ma-zi) “he has known her”, ilmassima; iḫḫazzi “he shall take her”; išakkanūši “they shall set her (on a stake)”
__broaden__.-šu: his / him · -šum “to him, for him” (dative): išakkanūšum, innadnušum · after a dental the suffix is assimilated and spelled with z: …ssu (ṣibat-zu, ṣibassu “its interest”, written after a broken sign); with a noun: ṣibtišu “its interest”, qātīšu “his hand”, damqaršu “his merchant”; tu-šu, te-šu in broken forms · with the same assimilation after a t: aššassu (aš-ša-zu) “his wife”, from aššat + -šu, t + š said ss · on a verb, the object “him”, or “to him” in the dative (Harper writes -šu for -šum): imaggarūšu (i-ma-ag-ga-ru-šu) “they shall agree to him”; on a noun after a preposition: elišu “upon him” · on a Š-stem, “him”: ušaḫḫazūšu “they shall have him take”, ušeṣṣûšu “they shall make him go out” · uktarriṣṣu (ug-dar-ri-zu) “he has slandered him” (ṣ + š said ṣṣ, spelled with ZU) · ikassûšuma “they shall bind him, and” · on nouns: emišu “his father-in-law’s”, ibiršu “his friend”, rabītišu “his senior one”, warkassu “his case”, zittišu “his share”, īnšu “his eye”
__broaden__.tirḫatum: bride-price, the marriage payment (understood as the groom’s gift): tirḫatum “the bride-price”, tirḫatiša “her bride-price” · tirḫatam, tirḫatim (tir-ḫa-tam, tir-ḫa-tim) “the bride-price”, the groom’s payment to the father-in-law, which is returned (utâr, uttēršum) or deducted from the dowry (iḫarraṣma)
__broaden__.warka: afterwards, later · as a conjunction before a clause, “after”: warka abum ana šīmtim ittalku “after the father has gone to his fate”
__broaden__.šeriqtum: dowry, what the bride brings from her father’s house (§138 ša ištu bīt abiša ublam “which she brought from her father’s house”): šeriqtam “the dowry”, šeriqtaša “her dowry”. Harper reads it with q (še-ri-iq-ta-ša, the sign IG read iq) and later editions with k; UNCERTAIN in the form, the meaning rests on §138 · šeriqtiša (še-ri-iq-ti-ša) “her dowry”, šeriqti (še-ri-iq-ti, construct) “the dowry of”: šeriqtaša ša mārīšama “her dowry is her children’s alone”; šeriqtaša ša bīt abiša-ma “her dowry is her father’s house’s alone”
__broaden__.mārtum: daughter (written DUMU+ti): mārtišu “his daughter” · mārassu (DUMU.SAL-zu, three signs DUMU + SAL + ZU, ZU for -ssu) “his daughter” · mārtaka (DUMU.SAL-ka) “your daughter”, mārtī (DUMU.SAL-i) “my daughter”, mārtim (DUMU.SAL, no ending written) “of the daughter”: abī mārtim “the father of the daughter”
__broaden__.mārum: son (DUMU) — here: a minor, not yet able to sell · member of a group: mārū ugārim (DUMU A.GÀR{meš}) “the sons of the irrigated land”, the district’s farmers · mār awīlim “a man’s son” (DUMU); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “sons” (oblique plural, which may include daughters, so “children”); māršu (DUMU-šu) “his son” · mārūša (DUMU{meš}-ša) “her sons” (nominative plural + suffix); mārīša (DUMU-ša) “her son” (genitive + suffix): ana mārīša “to her son” · mārī (DUMU-i) “my son” (-ī “my”); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “children” in mārī ūlissum “children she bore him”; mārū (DUMU{meš}) “sons” as subject: mārū ana ummātim ul izuzzū “the sons shall not divide by mothers”
__broaden__.aššatum: wife: ana aššatišu “to his wife” · aššassu (SAL-zu, ZU for -ssu) “his wife” · construct aššat (aš-ša-at) “wife of” before a genitive: aššat awīlim · aššatam, aššatim, aššatum, written SAL (the same sign as zinništum “woman”) or aš-ša-tam · aššātim (aš-ša-tim) “wives”, the plural (aššātim iḫuz “he has taken wives”; the signs could also spell the singular aššatim)
__broaden__.nadûm: to cast, throw (a charge; a body into the river): iddi, nadû, iddû · also to leave lying (a field): ittadi “he has left (it) lying” · of a flock: ṣēnī ana eqlim iddi “he turned the sheep loose into a field” · inaddûši (i-na-[ad]-du-u-ši) “they shall throw her” (present, plural, with -ši): ana mê inaddûši “they shall throw her into the water” · inaddûši “they shall throw him” of a man (§155, ana mê inaddûši), UNCERTAIN because the suffix -ši is “her” elsewhere
__broaden__.šakānum: to set, place: išakkanūšumma “they shall set for him (a term), and” · išakkanūšum (present, plural, dative -šum) “they shall place (it) for him”, i.e. count it to him · iššakkan (iš-ša-ak-ka-an, N-stem present) “it shall be put”: ul iššakkan “it shall not be put (in the account)” · to set, put, impose: ištakan (iš-ta-ka-an, perfect, “has set”), išakkan (present) — išakkanšima (i-ša-ak-ka-an-ši-ma, with -ši and -ma) “he/she shall set (it) on her, and”, as in abbuttam išakkan · išakkanūši “they shall set (her on a stake)”, išakkanūšumma “they shall set (it) aside for him, and” · idiom panam šakānum (panam ištakan) “to set the face” = to make up one’s mind
__broaden__.wabālum: to bring, carry: itbalam “he brought”, lū ublam “let me bring” · ublū (preterite, plural, in a ša-clause) “(the water) carried off” · ublam “he has brought”; lā ublam “he has not brought (on himself)”; ublu (ub-lu) “(which) he brought” (the relative -u); ubbalū (ub-ba-lu) “they shall carry”: panīšu ubbalū “they shall carry his face” = overlook it (UNCERTAIN idiom)
__broaden__.wabālum-Š: Š-stem of wabālum “to carry”: to make carry off, let (water) carry away: uštābil (perfect) “he has let (the water) carry off” · ušābilšu (u-ša-bil-šu, preterite) “he had (him) carry”; šūbulu (šu-bu-lu, Š stative šūbul with the subjunctive -u) “(what) has been sent”, šūbulūma (šu-bu-lu-ma) “has been sent, and”; the stative reading is from the form and the exact sense is UNCERTAIN · ušābil (u-ša-bi-il) “he has had (a present) brought” (preterite, without -u where there is no ša); ušābilu (u-ša-bi-lu) “who had (a present) brought” (with the relative -u)
__broaden__.nadānum: to give, pay: inaddin, iddinam, iddinušum; nadānim “to give” · iddin “he gave”; ana kaspim nadānum “to sell”: inaddinūma (present, plural) “they shall sell, and …” · iddin, iddinu “he gave” (preterite; the subjunctive -u in a ša- or inūma clause); iddinma “he gave, and”; …in, …din in broken forms; inaddin “he shall give”: ana damqaršu inaddin “he shall give to his merchant” · ittadinma (it-ta-di-in-ma) “he has given, and” (perfect); inaddinu (i-na-ad-di-nu) “(which) he gives” (present, with the subjunctive -u) · ittandin (it-ta-an-di-in, perfect with an extra -n-) “he has handed over”: ana kiššātim ittandin “he handed over into service”; ittadin (it-ta-din) “he has given”, i.e. sold; ana maṣṣarūtim inaddin “he gives for safekeeping”; iddinūšumma “they gave him, and” · inaddin also of a woman, “she shall give” · inaddišši (i-na-ad-di-iš-ši) “he/she shall give her” (the n of the stem swallowed before -ši), of a sale: ana kaspim inaddišši “she may sell her”, ul inaddišši “she shall not sell her” · anaddin “I shall give”, with the n merged into the k of -kum: anaddikkum (a-na-ad-di-ik-kum) “I shall give (her) to you”; iddinu (id-di-nu) “(which) he gave”; iddinušum “he gave him”
__broaden__.waṣûm-Š: Š-stem of waṣûm “to go out”: to send out, bring out; of land, to take on lease: ana irrišūtim ušēṣi “he took (a field) for cultivation” · ušeṣṣûšu (u-še-iz-zu-u-šu) “they shall make him go out” (present plural + -šu “him”; Harper writes ṣ as z): ālam ušeṣṣûšu “they shall drive him out of the city”
__broaden__.sūnum: lap, bosom: sūniša “her lap” (written zu-ni-ša); ina sūniša ittatīl “he lay in her lap” · sūn (zu-un) construct, “the lap of”: ina sūn ummišu “in the lap of his mother”
__broaden__.kasûm: to bind, tie up (probable, not certain; Harper’s i-ka-zu has the ZU sign, read su): ikassûšunūtima “they shall bind them” (-šunūti “them”, -ma “and”) · ikassûšuma (i-ka-zu-šu-ma) “they shall bind him, and” (-šu “him”, -ma “and”)
__broaden__.qalûm: to burn (Harper qalû): iqallû(ši) “they shall burn (her)” · iqallûšunūti (i-qal-lu-u-šu-nu-ti) “they shall burn them” (present plural + -šunūti “them”)
__broaden__.šunūti: them (masculine plural, accusative): ṣarrūtim šunūti “those criminals” · as the verbal suffix -šunūti “them”: iqallûšunūti “they shall burn them”
__broaden__.kilallān: both (of two): kilallašunu (ki-la-la-šu-nu) “both of them”, with -šunu “their, of them” · kilallīšunu (ki-la-li-šu-nu) “both of them” (Harper writes li here, la elsewhere)
__broaden__.rabûm: great; D/Š-stems “make great”; rabûtim “great (pl.)” · rabîtim (ra-bi-tim, feminine genitive) “large”: ina abnim rabîtim “by the large stone” · rabītišu (ra-bi-ti-šu) “his senior one”, the feminine with -šu: read as the father’s chief wife, UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.walādum: to bear, give birth to: ūlidušum (ul-du-šum) “(whom) she bore to him” (preterite ūlid, the long ū of a w-initial verb, with the subjunctive -u and the dative -šum; Harper’s spelling is shortened, so the vowels of the form are UNCERTAIN) · ittalad (it-ta-la-ad, perfect) “she has borne” · ūlid (u-li-id, preterite) “she bore”, ūldu (ul-du, with subjunctive -u) · ūlissum (u-li-zum) “she bore him” (ūlid + -šum, d and š said ss; the last sign is one complex sign, its identification UNCERTAIN) · waldat (wa-al-da-at) “she has borne” (stative): ša mārī waldat “who has borne children”
__broaden__.alākum: to go: illak “he shall go” · illiku “(where) he went” (preterite, subjunctive -u, after a restored ašar), in the agent law · alākišu (a-la-ki-šu) “his going” (infinitive with -šu): ina alākišu “in his going” · Gt present ittallak (it-ta-al-la-ak) “she shall go away” (the Gt gives the sense of going off; the Gtn would be ittanallak) · ittalak “she has gone” (perfect): ana šīmtim ittalak “she has gone to her fate” · ittalku (it-ta-al-ku) with the subjunctive -u: warka abum ana šīmtim ittalku “after the father has gone to his fate”
__broaden__.īnum: eye: īnšu … iššīma “he lifted his eye (to it)” — he coveted it · ša īnšu maḫru (i-in-šu) “whose eye is first” = the son he favours (UNCERTAIN idiom)
__broaden__.maḫrûm: first, former, previous: maḫrītim in šattim maḫrītim “in the previous year” · maḫru (maḫ-ru) “first, foremost” (an adjective or a stative of maḫārum): ša īnšu maḫru, read “the son he favours” (UNCERTAIN)
__broaden__.šarākum: to give away, hand over: ištarak · išruk (iš-ru-uq) “he has given (as a gift)” (the last sign UG, read uq or uk)
__broaden__.šaṭārum: to write; to assign in writing, deed over (Harper: išaddar): ul išaddar “he shall not deed” · išṭuršum (iš-tur-šum) “he wrote for him”: kunukkam išṭuršum “he wrote him a sealed document”
__broaden__.leqûm: to take: ileqqi “he shall take” · ilqi “he took” (il-qi₂), ilqû (subjunctive, il-qu₂-u₂), ilqēma (il-qi₂-e-ma) “he took, and”, ilteqēma (perfect, il-te-qi₂-ma) “he has taken, and”; ša … ilqû “which he took” · ilqēma (il-qi₂-ma) “he took, and” (preterite ilqe + -ma, here without a spelled e); ilteqe (il-te-qi₂, perfect) “he has taken”; ileqqi (i-li-qi₂, present) “he shall take”; leqîm (li-qi₂-im, infinitive, genitive): ina kaspim leqîm “in the taking of the silver” · ileqqûma (i-li-qu₂-ma) “they shall take, and” (present plural + -ma); ileqqēma “he shall take, and”
__broaden__.rašûm: to get, acquire: irtaši “he has acquired”, iraššû “he acquires” · iršû (ir-šu-u) “(whom) he has acquired” (the relative -u): ana mārī ša iršû “for the sons whom he has acquired”
__broaden__.pānum: front, face: ina pani “in front of” · panīša ištakan “she has set her face”: the idiom for making up one’s mind, resolving to do something; with ana + infinitive “to …” (panīšu, panīša “his, her face”) · idioms: panam šakānum “to set the face” = to make up one’s mind; panīšu wabālum “to carry his face” = to overlook an offence (UNCERTAIN)
__broaden__.parāsum: to decide, cut off: iprus · iparrasūma (i-par-ra-su-ma) “they shall investigate, and” (present plural + -ma; Harper: “to decide, to investigate, to inquire into”)
__broaden__.ištēn: one: šattam ištiatma “one year only” · ištiššu (iš-ti-iš-šu) “for the first time” (ištēn + -šu)
__broaden__.adi: up to, times: adi 12-šu “twelvefold” · as a conjunction, “as long as”, with the subjunctive: adi kirâm ṣabtu “as long as he holds the orchard” · adu 3-šu, adu 6-šu “three times, six times (as much)” — the multiplier, spelled a-du (Harper’s variant of adi; the plate has the sign DU) · adi šinīšu “up to his second time” = a second time (as adi 10-šu “tenfold”)
__broaden__.kaspum: silver — the code’s money, written KÙ.BABBAR “shining precious-metal” · kaspim: mišil mana kaspim “half a mina of silver” · with a spelled vowel after the logogram: KÙ.BABBAR-a-am, -i-im, -u-um: kaspam, kaspim, kaspum (accusative, genitive, nominative); kaspum as the subject; the grain-and-silver pair šeʾam u kaspam “grain and silver” · kasap (KÙ.BABBAR, no ending written) construct “silver of”: kasap tirḫatim “silver of the bride-price”
__broaden__.abum: father: ilik abišu “his father’s fief-duty” · abī (a-bi) construct “father of”: abī mārtim “the father of the daughter” · abim written a-ba in bīt abim (Harper’s spelling, UNCERTAIN)
__broaden__.ummum: mother: ana ummišu “to his mother”, ummašu urabbāšu “his mother shall raise him” · ummātim (um-ma-tim) plural “mothers”: ana ummātim “by mothers”; ummātišunu “their mothers”
__broaden__.bēlum: owner, lord: bēl ḫulqim “owner of the lost property” · owner of a field, bēl eqlim; bēl ḫubullim “creditor” · bēl kirîm “owner of the orchard” · bēl (be-el), the construct “owner of”, also with a suffix on the noun that follows: bēl ḫubullišu “his creditor”, bēl ḫubulliša “her creditor” · bēl (be-el, not the sign EN) “owner of”: bēl aššatim “the owner of the wife”, i.e. the man entitled to her (my reading)
__broaden__.ragāmum: to claim, to call out a claim: irgumu (ir-gu-mu, preterite with the subjunctive -u) “(whatever) he claimed” · iraggum (i-ra-ag-gu-um) “he shall claim” (present with the ventive -m): ul iraggum “he shall not claim”
__broaden__.tabālum: to take away, carry off: itabbal · tabal “take!” (imperative) · itbal (it-ba-al, preterite) “he took away” · itbalam (it-ba-lam, preterite + the ventive -am) “he has brought (it)”, the form that serves for “bring on”: ana abišu itbalam “he has brought (it) to his father”
